newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Ceramco sees 6 mth loss, year break-even.
newsitem.headline: Ceramco sees 6 mth loss, year break-even.

text.p: New Zealand's Ceramco Corp Ltd said on Thursday it expects a net loss of NZ$1.6 million for the six months to September 30 but a break even for the year.
It said the previously announced sale of the Klipper & John Webster division was now unlikely to proceed.
Ceramco said a continuing failure to meet budgeted sales would significantly affect apparel operations for the year ended March 31.
NZ China Clays was trading satisfactorily and should exceed last year's result for the year.
"This will not be sufficient to offset the deterioration of results in the apparel group," Ceramco said in a statement.
Measures had been taken both to reduce costs within the apparel division and to stimulate demand for its products.
These actions would result in non recurring restructuring costs of $800,000 after tax which will affect the group's results for the 1997 financial year.
"It is anticipated that a net loss after tax of $1.6 million will be incurred for the six months ended September 30."
For the second six months, Ceramco is projecting a return to profitability and forecasting a break even result for the full year, after tax and non recurring items.
Ceramco said it was extremely conscious that today's announcement was the latest in a series of profit downgrades.

"Shareholders can be assured that remedial action is being taken and that the board will take whatever steps are required in order to restore the apparel business to an acceptable level of profitability."
A new managing director for Bendon Hickory Ltd will be appointed.
The board had resolved to appoint the new Chairman, David Appleby, as Executive Chairman of the Group.
Rod Inglis, a director, is to be involved for a limited period in reviewing the apparel sales and marketing operations and the positioning of the various brands owned by Bendon Hickory.
Ceramco said it remains of the view that the long term outlook for the apparel brands was positive.
"It will however take a period of focused activity and further change before profits are restored to satisfactory levels." -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
